name: PostgreSQL (archived reference server)
upstream_status_note: The repository is archived (read-only) on GitHub. The npm record marks the package deprecated. Quoted: “Archived and unmaintained; no security guarantees. See https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived”. The repository's own README says it is no longer maintained. Quoted: “This repository is archived and no longer maintained.”.
outcome_statement: As of 2026-11-14: meets C4, C5, C7; partly meets C1, C2, C8, C10; does not meet C3, C6, C9.

findings.title: Source and release provenance
findings.finding: The npm record for @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres@0.6.2 has no repository field; its deprecation notice names the archive repository. The record carries no provenance attestation. Quoted: “Archived and unmaintained; no security guarantees. See https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived”.

findings.title: Published security policy
findings.finding: GitHub shows a security policy for the repository (`SECURITY.md`); the policy says the repository is no longer covered by a vulnerability disclosure programme. Quoted: “This archived repository is no longer covered by our vulnerability disclosure program.”.

findings.title: Maintenance status
findings.finding: The repository is archived (read-only) on GitHub. The npm record marks the package deprecated. Quoted: “Archived and unmaintained; no security guarantees. See https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived”. The repository's own README says it is no longer maintained. Quoted: “This repository is archived and no longer maintained.”. Latest release 0.6.2 is dated 2024-12-04; the newest commit on `main` is dated 2025-05-28; GitHub reports the last push on 2025-05-28.

findings.title: Published advisories
findings.finding: No advisory is published in the repository's advisory list for @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres.

findings.title: Documented scope controls
findings.finding: The README describes the single tool as read-only. Quoted: “All queries are executed within a READ ONLY transaction”.

findings.title: Credential handling in the documented setup
findings.finding: The only documented setup passes the database address as a command-line argument, and the README says the user name and password can be placed in it. Quoted: “username/password can be added to the postgresql url with `postgresql://user:password@host:port/db-name`”; “postgresql://localhost/mydb”.

findings.title: Telemetry and outbound data, as documented
findings.finding: The README contains no reference to telemetry or usage collection, and the documented function contacts only the service the user configures. Searched `src/postgres/README.md` for: telemetry, usage statistics, usage stats, we collect, data collection, opt-out, posthog.

findings.title: Dependency management files
findings.finding: A lockfile (`package-lock.json`) is committed. No Dependabot or Renovate configuration file exists at the paths listed in the methodology.

findings.title: Documentation of untrusted-content risk
findings.finding: No statement about prompt injection or untrusted content was found in the files searched. Searched `src/postgres/README.md` for: prompt-injection, untrusted, malicious, attacker, adversarial; `SECURITY.md` for: prompt-injection, untrusted.

findings.title: Currency of the declared MCP library
findings.finding: Declared MCP library: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.0.1. Lower-bound version 1.0.1 of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (npm) was published on 2024-11-26, between 12 and 24 months before 2026-11-14.

third_party_reports.title: MCP vulnerability case study: SQL injection in the Postgres MCP server
third_party_reports.status: reported by Datadog Security Labs, not confirmed in the project's own material
